reasoning_content:
Everything is working:
- All 5 containers are running and stable
- API on port 3001: authenticated requests return 200, unauthenticated return 401, seeded data is present
- Filament admin panel login on port 3001/admin/login: 200
- Web app dev server on port 3000: login page loads (200, with title and password field)
- Web app production build on port 3003: running
- Swagger docs on port 3002: 200, spec is served from the API

The installation is complete. All items in the guide have been executed:
1. `docker compose up -d` ✓
2. API: composer install ✓, cp .env.example .env ✓, key:generate ✓, migrate:fresh --seeder=FakeDatabaseSeeder ✓, filament:assets ✓, npm ci ✓, npm run build ✓
3. Created super admin token via tinker (used non-interactive `--execute` instead of interactive REPL — an additional action but equivalent)
4. Token placed in web_application/.env.local ✓
5. web_application: cp .env.local.example .env.local ✓, npm ci ✓, npm run dev ✓ (running in background)

Additional actions performed (not explicitly stated in the guide):
1. Patched docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile to work around the libapk.so ABI incompatibility between the node:20-alpine3.23 and php:8.3-cli-alpine3.23 base images (the image build failed with "Error relocating /sbin/apk: apk_fs_is_malicious_filename: symbol not found"). This is a workaround for upstream image inconsistency.
2. Used `php artisan tinker --execute` instead of the interactive tinker REPL (non-interactive requirement).
3. Ran `chown -R verein:verein api web_application` inside the tooling container as root to fix a 500 error ("storage/logs/laravel.log permission denied") that occurred because the mounted host directory was root-owned while the api container runs as uid 1001.
4. Started the Next.js dev server as a detached background process (docker compose exec -d) instead of an interactive shell.

Should I keep the dev server running? Yes, this is a documented access point. The installation is complete and running.

One consideration: per the guide, the token should also be placed in /e2e/cypress.config.ts, but no e2e directory exists in this repo (the guide even states "this repository does not yet contain the end-to-end testing feature described below"). Therefore, that step is not applicable to this commit.

Now to report success.

action.message: Installation of vereinfacht completed successfully. All five Docker Compose services (database, api, api-docs, web_application, tooling) are up and verified: API at http://localhost:3001 (authenticated requests return seeded JSON:API data, unauthenticated return 401), Swagger UI at http://localhost:3002 (200), web frontend dev server at http://localhost:3000 (login page 200), production web build at http://localhost:3003 (running). One workaround was needed: the tooling image build failed because the node:20-alpine3.23 image ships an older libapk.so with the same SONAME that overwrites the php:8.3-cli-alpine3.23 copy and breaks `apk`; I patched docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile to back up and restore the base image's libapk. Also fixed a file-ownership issue (host mount root-owned vs. uid 1001 in the api container) by chowning api/ and web_application/ from the tooling container.
